scores.why: Ten sheets are respected, but the creative review and pilot conditions contain too much presentation-layer text for a joint CMO/CFO reading.

fixes.quote: Six blocking open items from the brief:
fixes.change: Replace the visible six-item list with a one-line summary linked to the existing detailed checklist.
Reduce each decision to action, owner, deadline and release condition; keep measurement procedures and cost categories in the ledger.

fixes.quote: This sheet is the summary. Sheet 02 is the product; sheets 03–09 the evidence; sheet 10 the decisions.
fixes.change: Delete this explanation because the executive route immediately above already provides the reading map.

scores.why: The essential evidence, usage, risks and decision owners are covered, but readers cannot inspect the complete deliverable and the pilot lacks its documented transcript contingency.

fixes.quote: Embedded extracts are shown here; complete source documents remain in the repository.
fixes.change: Embed the complete Greek and English briefs in collapsed reference sections so the standalone file contains the actual deliverable.

fixes.quote: Weeks 2–3: two leads review three past projects each.
fixes.change: Add the PRD §8 contingency to the pilot ledger: confirm transcript availability in week 1 and use the documented prospective kickoff plan if full transcripts are unavailable.

scores.why: The AI/code/people distinction is strong, but technical shorthand and competing attention-time definitions still require interpretation.

fixes.quote: Re-baseline usage and time under the 30 July routing before week 1: larger extraction model plus second reader.
fixes.change: Use: “Before week 1, measure usage and time again with the model choices adopted on 30 July: a larger extraction model and a second AI checker.”
Label this explicitly as a proposed review-time target requiring sponsor agreement, distinct from the PRD’s time-to-first-draft metric.

scores.why: The answer-first sequence and evidence-backed titles work well, but the closing sheet reopens an already demonstrated budget example instead of ending cleanly on the pilot decision.

fixes.quote: The budget stays «κάπου στα ογδόντα»: no invented or resolved total in the brief or either render. Shadow Draft A invented one; the creative lead strikes it.
fixes.change: Keep this evidence on sheets 05–09 and replace the closing passage with the immediate kickoff action: assign the sponsor and operator, then complete the three pre-start conditions.

scores.why: Brief Builder has a credible promise, operating boundary and ownership model, but its principles and manual approval mechanics are more buried than a buyer needs.

fixes.quote: Ask, don’t guess · Surface, don’t resolve · Flag, don’t correct · Look up, don’t invent · Sign, don’t send
fixes.change: Promote this compact principles line from the ledger into the visible product overview.

fixes.quote: The account lead records resolutions and signature in brief.json. brief_review.html displays those recorded decisions.
fixes.change: State plainly that v1 approval requires manually editing a structured file and that the review page has no save or approval control.

scores.why: The source defines a coherent editorial system and restrained palette, but the creative and decision sheets leave substantial width unused while stacking lengthy material.

fixes.change: Give these sheets dedicated desktop layouts that use the empty sidebar area for artwork or decision ownership instead of retaining an unused quarter-width column.
Position the creative illustration beside the concise A/B assessment near the top, with the extended brief below or collapsed.

scores.why: The checked model IDs, 983 820 stage-one tokens, 1 134 734 total tokens, approximately 33 minutes, 17 checks and de-duplicated cost match the repository, with assumptions and known discrepancies disclosed.
Self-contained assets, navigation, focus handling and responsive rules are thoughtfully implemented, but read-all navigation can lose correspondence with the sheet being viewed.

fixes.change: Update the current-sheet state as readers scroll in read-all mode so Contents, Next and Back follow the visible sheet.
Add a compact keyboard hint explaining left/right arrows and how to open and dismiss Contents.

scores.why: The embedded can is appealing and honestly labelled, and the brief exposes its errors, but the vertical artwork knowingly leaves the brand lockup in the caption zone.

fixes.quote: 9:16 still frame at the TikTok in-feed spec; the lockup sits in TikTok’s caption zone, a dedicated 9:16 layout would raise it
fixes.change: Create a dedicated vertical illustration with the lockup raised into the usable area, preserving brand clear space and the mock-up label.

fixes.quote: A or B, or neither: a creative lead must evaluate the shadow drafts. Owner and decision date remain unassigned.
fixes.change: Make assigning the creative lead a kickoff action and consolidate the evaluation deadline here as before week 4.

overall: Credible evidence and governance; not yet ready to ship unchanged because the final two sheets need compression and clearer visual priority. Hash verified; no repository files edited. Visual and UX scores rely on source inspection and the embedded can image: both local browser-render attempts failed.
